NONE: B1 UK US rent to pay to use something for a short period
B2 to employ someone or pay someone to do a particular job

U: › [ U ] UK an arrangement to use something by paying for it

C: › [ C ] mainly US a person to whom a company has recently given a job

example: How much would it cost to hire a car for the weekend?
租一輛車週末用要多少錢？
You could always hire a dress for the ball if you can't afford to buy one.
如果你買不起舞會禮服，起碼可以租一套。
I was hired by the first company I applied to.
我應徵的第一家公司僱用了我。
[ + to infinitive ] We ought to hire a public relations consultant to help improve our image.
我們應該僱用一位公共關係顧問來提升我們的形象。
The price includes flights and car hire.
此價格包含機票和租車的費用。
a hire car
租借用車
There's a camping shop in town that has tents for hire (= available to be hired) at £30 a week.
城裡有家露營用品店有帳篷可供出租，費用為每週三十英鎊。
See also
rent
She's our latest hire.
她是我們最新的僱員。

NONE: › a method of paying for something in which the buyer pays part of the cost immediately and then makes small regular payments until the debt is completely paid
› to allow someone to use something or someone temporarily in exchange for money

example: UK How much do you charge for hiring out a bicycle for a week?
租一輛腳踏車一個星期需要多少錢？
He's decided to go freelance and hire himself out as a technical writer.
他決定做自由作家，從事科技文章撰稿。

NONE: › someone who has been persuaded by an offer of money to do an unpleasant or unpopular job

example: He's not the boss, he's just a hireling employed to do the dirty work.
他不是老闆，只是被僱來做那些卑鄙的勾當。

NONE: › the act of starting to employ someone

example: The office has completely changed in the past few weeks because there have been so many hirings and firings (= a lot of new people have been employed and a lot of others have lost their jobs).
過去幾週裡，辦公室發生了徹底的改變，請了不少新人，也解僱了不少人。

NONE: › having a lot of hair, especially on the face or body
